passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Study A tested a reading app with 400 second-graders for one school year.
• Students using the app gained 8 points on a reading test.
• Students in a comparison group gained 7 points.
• The difference was not statistically significant.
stem: The student wants to present the study's results accurately to readers who might assume the app was highly effective. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: Although app users gained 8 points and the comparison group 7, the difference was not statistically significant.
Students using the reading app gained 8 points on a reading test over a school year.
A study tested a reading app with 400 second-graders for an entire school year.
The reading app helped the 400 second-graders who used it gain more points on a reading test than students in the comparison group.
steps: Accuracy for skeptical-of-effect readers requires the comparison and the lack of significance.
Only the first choice gives both groups' gains and the key caveat.
The second and fourth suggest an effect without the caveat; the third gives no results.
key: “Accurately” usually means including the qualification that limits a result.
source: SAT AIS original item, written to the College Board Digital SAT content specifications
